## How GRACE Follow-On Tracks Changes in Earth’s Water

Launched in 2018, GRACE Follow-On consists of two spacecraft that follow one another about 137 miles (220 kilometers) apart. The mission uses changes in the distance between them to infer shifts in mass on Earth.

As the pair approaches a larger mass concentration, gravity acts on the leading spacecraft first, initially pulling it farther from the trailing spacecraft. The resulting change in their separation is the measurement—not a direct image of water.

Scientists use the inferred mass shifts to investigate changes in groundwater, lakes and rivers, soil moisture, glaciers and ice sheets, and sea level associated with water added to the oceans.
